slot-81d3aa0c-987d-431d-b67d-f46b8df866d.quote_span: A federal judge ruled Wednesday that two police officers who defended the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021, have no standing to sue over their names — and those of other first responders — not appearing on a plaque commemorating law enforcement’s response to the attack.
slot-81d3aa0c-987d-431d-b67d-f46b8df866d.speaker: The Hill
slot-81d3aa0c-987d-431d-b67d-f46b8df866d.checkable_against: U.S. District Court ruling on the Jan. 6 memorial plaque lawsuit

slot-3f8b2628-cb5b-4e55-b1a7-20c7bad2eb3.quote_span: Former President Biden signed a law in 2022 requesting a plaque to honor the officers who defended the Capitol during the attack, giving its installation a one-year deadline. But the plaque was never erected.
slot-3f8b2628-cb5b-4e55-b1a7-20c7bad2eb3.speaker: outlet's own
slot-3f8b2628-cb5b-4e55-b1a7-20c7bad2eb3.checkable_against: 2022 federal law concerning a plaque honoring Jan. 6 Capitol defenders
